text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds futures were nearly unchanged in late trade, but outperformed other bond markets on the day as the strong mark made German investments more attractive. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.27, down 0.06 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts slid again on Thursday, widening the spread over Bunds to an eight-month high and seeing Italian BTPs trade through them for the first time ever. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-18/32, down 26/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures slipped slightly on Thursday, largely driven by weaker bond markets in Germany and the U.S., but managed to hold on to most of the heady gains made in the past two sessions. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.28 down 0.10 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended easier but off session lows following other markets but with nothing concrete providing direction. The Italian market is seen consolidating after recent days' strong gains. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.40 down 0.30 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened sharply lower, dragged down by a strong dollar and debt securities sell-off overnight after bearish comments by a Japanese Finance Minister official. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-3/32, down 17/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.65 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures took a dive on Thursday, pulled down by sales of cash JGBs and comments by a senior Finance Ministry official. "Large financial institutions were detected making sales," a city bank trader said. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.67, down 1.10 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - LONDON - Mexico's first floating-rate lira offering stood out on Thursday morning amid another round of issuance in a wide range of sectors and structures. Mexico's expected 500 billion lire five-year FRN was priced at a margin of 210 b.p. over three-month LIBOR via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and J.P. Morgan Securities.
